plan:
FINAL EXPERIMENT DESIGN (design-only; nothing executed)

## 1) Objective as testable claims
C1 (complexity): On identical settings and the same torchviz extraction, the autograd graph that contains a fused TorchOpt Adam update has strictly fewer op-nodes (N_ops), edges (E), distinct op types, and no greater op-depth than the graph containing an equivalent non-fused Adam update.
C2 (interpretability, structural proxy): The fused graph has lower op-type entropy H and a lower fraction of primitive update ops U than the non-fused graph.
C3 (fallback premise check): In the CPU-runnable configuration, the TorchOpt update actually appears as a collapsed node (single custom op); if not, C1/C2 are evaluated on the hand-written single-node control instead (see §4).

## 2) Rationale / hypothesis
Fusion collapses the ~k elementwise autograd ops of one Adam step (m, v, bias-corrected m̂/ν̂, sqrt+eps, division, weight update) into a single custom op with a defined vjp (TorchOpt custom_vjp; equivalently a user autograd.Function). Fewer nodes/edges/types ⇒ shorter description of the graph ⇒ structurally "less complex and more interpretable". Interpretability is proxied exactly as description-length and op-type diversity, not human judgment. Prediction: for the update portion N_ops(unfused) ≈ #params·k vs ≈ #params(fused) ⇒ ratio ≈ 1/k, k≈8–12 for Adam.

## 3) Experimental setup
Models (all seed 0, fixed input): MLP with ReLU, sweep width w∈{16,64,256} × depth d∈{2,3,5}; one Conv net (2 conv + 2 linear). Batch 8, deterministic input/target; loss = MSE to a fixed random target.
Adam semantics (must MATCH across all conditions): lr=1e-3, betas=(0.9,0.999), eps=1e-8, weight_decay=0 (and a second run with weight_decay=1e-4 because torch.optim and TorchOpt differ in L2 handling); bias correction ON, amsgrad OFF, no foreach/capturable. Set TorchOpt to the differentiable/custom_vjp path (CPU-valid); record the exact option names used at install time.
Update-in-graph construction (critical): torch.optim.step() is in-place and leaves NO autograd trace, so it cannot be compared. Every condition therefore materializes the update as a differentiable function of (params, grads, state) producing new_params, and make_dot is run on the SAME representative output tensor (updated first-layer weight) in all conditions, so update ops are visible and comparable. Baseline non-fused (A) = a manual transcription of the classic Adam formula in plain autograd ops (graph-visible, non-fused). Fused TorchOpt (B) = same formula via TorchOpt's differentiable Adam (expected single custom node). Control (C) in §4.
make_dot pinned: make_dot(y, params=...) with show_attrs=False, truncate=False (fixed in ALL runs); parse dot.to_string() text with pydot/graphviz python (installed as part of setup).
Node/edge counting convention (reproducible): op-node = DOT node whose label contains an operation class name (Pattern "*Backward0" for built-ins, or the TorchOpt/custom fused class name); tensor-node = every other node (leaf/param/const tensor labels, no op-class name). N_ops = #op-nodes; N_nodes = N_ops + #tensor-nodes; E = #DOT edges; op-depth = longest root→output path measured in op-nodes; distinct_op_types = #unique op-class names among op-nodes. update_subgraph = op-nodes present in the make_dot(updated_weight) graph but absent from make_dot(loss-of-updated-weight) graph (i.e., optimizer-only ops); update_op_fraction = |update_subgraph| / N_ops.

## 4) Controls
- C1 (fusion isolation, the core control given CPU): a hand-written single torch.autograd.Function "AdamStep" implementing the exact Adam math in one forward/one vjp (one op-node) vs. the manual multi-op transcription (A). Any metric delta between C1 and A is attributable to node collapse alone, independent of TorchOpt hardware.
- C2 (real package): TorchOpt differentiable Adam (B) vs. A — verifies the package realizes the same collapse.
- Sanity check: assert B's DOT contains ≥1 node labeled with the TorchOpt/custom fused class name; if B does NOT show a collapsed node on CPU, then C1 replaces B for the headline claims and the design reports that TorchOpt fusion is not realized in the CPU-runnable configuration (premise fails for that config).
- C3 (reference only): torch.optim.Adam.step() and torch.optim.fused.Adam (if importable/runnable on CPU; fused is CUDA-oriented and may be unavailable) traced on the updated-param copy, to document that in-place steps leave near-leaf graphs; NOT used in the complexity comparison.

## 5) Metrics and analysis / decision rule
Per config (model×condition) compute {N_ops, E, op-depth, distinct_op_types, update_op_fraction, H=−Σpᵢlog₂pᵢ over op-type distribution, U=share of update_subgraph nodes that are primitive elementwise ops (Add/Mul/Sub/Pow/Sqrt/Div/…)}. H and U define the interpretability proxy: lower H and lower U ⇒ more interpretable.
Decision: SUPPORT if, over the full sweep, fused (B or C1) is ≤ baseline (A) on N_ops, E, distinct_op_types, op-depth in every config with strict improvement on N_ops somewhere, AND H_fused<H_A and U_fused<U_A throughout. PARTIAL if only complexity holds. NULL/NEGATIVE if op counts are equal or reversed, or if the premise check fails (no collapse on CPU) — in the latter case report "not less complex in the CPU-runnable configuration" and use C1 to state whether fusion per se would help if hardware-supported. Report per-point ratios and medians over the sweep; no significance machinery is required for a structural comparison, but report min/max spread for transparency.

## 6) Feasibility and limitations
- CPU-only, no GPU: TorchOpt accelerated/CUDA fused kernels unavailable; the differentiable/custom_vjp path (CPU-backed) and the hand-written autograd.Function control are used; hardware-dependent fusion claims are deferred.
- Workspace contains no TorchOpt/TorchViz sources and no packages; exact API names, make_dot signature, and graphviz bindings must be confirmed and pinned at install time (front-loaded check §4).
- Comparison is on parsed DOT structure only; Graphviz visual layout is not a metric.
- Interpretability is a structural/description-length proxy, NOT validated by a user study; C1/C2 claim scope is limited to this proxy.
- Semantics-matching (esp. weight_decay) is verified by running both wd=0 and wd=1e-4 and checking op sets stay comparable; discrepancies are reported, not hidden.
- No claimed results; everything above is the plan.

context.question: Does fusing operations within the Adam optimizer (as done in TorchOpt) result in a less complex and more interpretable gradient graph compared to the output from TorchViz?
context.context: Design an experiment that answers the question. The researcher can clarify source-supported setup details by topic. Do not claim that an experiment was run.
